**Title: The Feathered Leak**

Arthur Pendergast, a mid-level accountant with the charisma of a damp sponge, stood in the breakroom, sweating through his shirt. On his shoulder sat Barnaby, a macaw with a vocabulary range limited to corporate jargon and profanity. It was "Bring Your Pet to Work Day," and Arthur had made a catastrophic error in judgment.

Barnaby wasn’t just a pet; he was a recording device with feathers.

"Good morning, Arthur!" chirped Barnaby, flapping his wings. "Quarterly earnings are down! Fire the CEO! Buy more ducks!"

Arthur froze. The breakroom was empty, save for Brenda from HR, who was stirring her coffee with the intensity of a bomb disposal expert.

"Barnaby, hush," Arthur hissed, trying to cover the bird’s beak with his hand.

"Cover up the embezzlement!" Barnaby squawked, leaning into Arthur’s ear. "Shred the documents! The IRS is coming!"

Brenda stopped stirring. She turned slowly. "Arthur, did your bird just mention embezzlement?"

"No! No, Brenda, it’s... it’s a new trick! He’s learning from my stress levels!" Arthur laughed, a high-pitched sound that betrayed his panic. He grabbed Barnaby and shoved him into his briefcase. "He’s shy! He’s an introvert!"

Barnaby’s head popped out of the briefcase. "Introvert! Introvert! Also, the CEO’s wife knows about the offshore accounts!"

Arthur slammed the briefcase shut. "I’m going to take him to the conference room. For... bird therapy."

He sprinted to the conference room, locking the door behind him. He placed the briefcase on the table and opened it slightly. "Barnaby, listen to me. We are in a crisis. If you say one more word about the offshore accounts, I will turn you into a feather duster. Do you understand?"

Barnaby tilted his head. "Feather duster! Feather duster! Also, the server room password is 'password123'!"

Arthur’s blood ran cold. He had changed the server password yesterday. He hadn’t told anyone. Not even his mother.
